name: web.market
description: RIG market-fit gate for a sales page, built from the Sept 2026 Eden social sweep findings verified at source (Isenberg, Pierce, Torti, Saraev, Reimer): sell finished work, anchor against the human alternative, name the system, lead with one named pain, prefer boring reliable jobs, make the rulebook and accountability visible, and offer a diagnostic wedge. Input is an evidence dossier of observable page facts.

mkt_finished_work.instructions: Does the page sell a finished, checkable deliverable rather than a tool, an AI capability or automation itself? (family M, weight 3)
criteria: Sells technology or 'AI' itself; no deliverable named
Sells a service category (automation, AI consulting)
Names a tool stack or platform as the offer
Names a process area but not a finished output
Names a finished output in generic terms
Names one finished output a buyer could check
Finished output plus who receives and owns it
Finished output, owner, and acceptance test stated
Finished output with written acceptance and a sample shown
Every offer is a named, checkable finished job with a visible sample

mkt_human_alternative.instructions: Is the offer anchored against the human or status-quo alternative the buyer pays for today (staff hours, a hire, an agency, lost inquiries) without invented numbers? (family M, weight 2)
criteria: No comparison to any alternative
Vague 'save time and money'
Unsourced percentage savings
Names an alternative (hire, agency, freelancer) without its cost
Names the alternative and what it fails to do
Compares routes on accountability and ownership
Compares routes on cost structure, no invented figures
Gives the buyer a way to compute their own cost of the gap
Buyer-computable anchor plus a published price to compare against
Clear, honest comparison against the human alternative using the buyer's own numbers

mkt_named_system.instructions: Is the offering packaged as a named, bounded system whose named components each map to a business outcome? (family M, weight 2)
criteria: Unnamed list of services
Generic service names (Consulting, Automation)
One named offer, components unnamed
Named offer with a feature list
Named offer, components described as technology
Named components mapped to outcomes
Named system with outcomes and a scope boundary
Named system per buyer situation
Named system per vertical on a shared spine
Memorable named system per vertical, every component an outcome with an acceptance test

mkt_named_pain_lead.instructions: Does the page open with one named, specific pain the buyer already feels, before method or capability? (family M, weight 3)
criteria: Opens with the company or its technology
Opens with a slogan
Opens with a broad category problem
Names a problem area without a moment
Names a specific failure moment
Specific failure moment in the buyer's words
Specific pain plus its cost to the buyer
Specific pain, its cost, and who it happens to
A distinct pain per vertical, in that vertical's language
Opening pain so specific the target reader feels named, with the moment and the cost

mkt_boring_reliable_job.instructions: Does the offer lead with a boring, repeatable, checkable job rather than a flashy agent, chatbot or voice AI? (family M, weight 1)
criteria: Leads with chatbot, voice or agent novelty
Leads with 'AI transformation'
Novelty first, jobs second
Jobs first, novelty mixed in
One repeatable job named
Repeatable job with its frequency
Repeatable job and the failure it prevents
Repeatable job, failure prevented, and how it is checked
Several repeatable jobs ranked by reliability
Boring, checkable jobs are the whole pitch; novelty appears only as a component

mkt_rulebook_accountability.instructions: Does the page make its written rulebook (what 'correct' looks like) and personal accountability for mistakes a visible part of the product? (family M, weight 2)
criteria: No mention of standards or accountability
Generic 'quality' claim
Testing mentioned in passing
Says acceptance criteria exist
Shows some acceptance criteria
Shows a named list of tests
Test list plus who owns failures
Written definition of correct plus a named owner of mistakes
Rulebook shown, owner named, and what happens when it fails
Rulebook and accountability are the headline product, with a sample and a stated remedy

mkt_diagnostic_wedge.instructions: Is there a free or paid diagnostic that produces a standalone asset and a clear, stated path into the build? (family M, weight 2)
criteria: No diagnostic step
Free call only
Diagnostic mentioned, no output
Diagnostic with a vague output
Diagnostic with a named output
Priced diagnostic with a named output
Priced diagnostic, named output and timeline
Output usable without the vendor
Plus its relationship to the build price stated (credited or not)
Priced, time-boxed diagnostic whose output stands alone and whose credit toward the build is explicit

rules.reason: sells a tool or category, not a finished deliverable
no specific buyer pain in the opening
